Arthur Phillip (11 October 1738 - 31 August 1814) was a British Royal Navy officer who served as the first governor of the Colony of New South Wales.

Chin Peng (21 October 1924 - 16 September 2013), born Ong Boon Hua, was a Malayan communist politician, guerrilla leader, and revolutionary.

While working for the RAND Corporation, this military analyst leaked a top-secret Pentagon study on Vietnam War decision-making to major newspapers in 1971, later facing Espionage Act charges carrying up to 115 years — who is he?
Daniel Ellsberg (April 7, 1931 - June 16, 2023) was an American political activist, economist, and United States military analyst.

Eurocopter Tiger is a four-blade, twin-engine attack helicopter which first entered service in 2003.

J. E. B. Stuart (February 6, 1833 - May 12, 1864) was a Confederate cavalry general during the American Civil War.
This biblical queen, wife of King Ahab of Israel, was thrown from a window on the orders of Jehu and devoured by dogs, as the prophet Elijah had foretold — who was she?
Jezebel was the daughter of Ithobaal I of Tyre and the wife of Ahab, King of Israel, according to the Book of Kings of the Hebrew Bible (1 Kings 16).
This member of the First Triumvirate led the Gallic Wars, defeated Pompey, and sparked the political chaos that would end the Republic. Who?

Julius Caesar (12 or 13 July 100 BC - 15 March 44 BC) was a Roman general, statesman, and author who was the dictator of the Roman Republic almost continuously from 49 BC until his assassination in 44 BC.

Kingdom of Prussia was a German state that existed from 1701 to 1918.
Born in Karnal to a wealthy Rajput family, this lawyer became the first prime minister of his newly founded nation and, revered as 'Leader of the Nation,' was assassinated in 1951 — who was he?
Liaquat Ali Khan (1 October 1895 - 16 October 1951) was a Pakistani lawyer, politician and statesman who served as the first prime minister of Pakistan from 1947 until his assassination in 1951.

Serving as the third and last Commonwealth president for barely five weeks in 1946, this man then became the first leader of the newly independent Philippine republic before dying in office in 1948 — who was he?
Manuel Roxas (January 1, 1892 - April 15, 1948) was the fifth president of the Philippines, serving from 1946 until his death in 1948.
Described in Genesis as the king of Salem and a priest of 'God Most High,' this biblical figure blesses Abram with bread and wine and is later invoked in the Epistle to the Hebrews — who is he?
Melchizedek was the king of Salem and priest of El Elyon (often translated as "God Most High").
Serving as the sixth chief of a major right-wing Hindu nationalist organization since 2009, this Indian activist was born in 1950 — who is he?

Mohan Bhagwat (born 11 September 1950) is an Indian activist who is serving as the sixth and current Sarsanghchalak (Chief) of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), a right-wing Hindutva paramilitary organisation, since 2009.
Founded in 2023 by Pieter Omtzigt, what is the name of this Christian-democratic political party in the Netherlands?
New Social Contract is a Christian-democratic political party in the Netherlands founded by Pieter Omtzigt in 2023.
This November 1942 Allied invasion of French North Africa, a three-pronged strike at Casablanca, Oran and beyond, gave U.S. forces their first foothold against the Axis — what was it called?
Operation Torch (8-16 November 1942) was an Allied invasion of French North Africa during World War II.
Succeeding his father's abdication in 2013, this monarch is the eldest child of King Albert II and married Mathilde d'Udekem d'Acoz, with whom he has four children — who is he?
Philippe of Belgium (born 15 April 1960) is King of the Belgians, and is the eldest child of King Albert II and Queen Paola.
The first person from Uttar Pradesh and the first member of the BJP to hold the office, this Indian lawyer and politician served as his country's president from 2017 to 2022. Who is he?
Ram Nath Kovind (born 1 October 1945) is an Indian politician and lawyer who served as the president of India from 2017 to 2022.
Born in British Hong Kong and once a Member of Parliament, this academic and broadcaster now co-directs a grand-strategy program at Yale and co-hosts the podcast 'The Rest Is Politics' — who is he?
Rory Stewart (born 3 January 1973) is a British academic, broadcaster, writer, and former diplomat and politician.
This Austrian politician first became a government minister overseeing refugee integration in 2011, then served two separate terms as chancellor — who is he?
Sebastian Kurz (born 27 August 1986) is an Austrian former politician who served twice as Chancellor of Austria, first from 2017 to 2019 and then again from 2020 to 2021.
Documented in some form across Buddhism, Christianity, Vodou, Hinduism, Islam, and more, this altered state is attributed to control of the body by ghosts, demons, or deities — what is it called?
Spirit possession is an altered state of consciousness and associated behaviors purportedly caused by the control of a human body and its functions by spirits, ghosts, demons, angels, or deities.

Velvet Revolution was a non-violent transition of power in what was then Czechoslovakia, occurring from 17 November to 28 November 1989.
This British statesman began his political career as a Conservative MP for Newark but became the face of the Liberal Party, serving a record four non-consecutive terms as Prime Minister — who is he?
William Ewart Gladstone (29 December 1809 - 19 May 1898) was a British statesman who served four times as Prime Minister of the United Kingdom.
This Chinese statesman served as the first Premier of the People's Republic of China from 1949 until his death in 1976, doubling as foreign minister for the first nine years — who is he?

Asherah: Ancient Semitic goddess. Asherah was a major goddess in ancient Northwest Semitic cultures, often associated with fertility, motherhood, and sacred trees.

Brian Mulroney: Prime Minister of Canada from 1984 to 1993. Born in the eastern Quebec city of Baie-Comeau, Mulroney studied political science and law.

Catherine the Great: Empress of Russia from 1762 to 1796.

Cornwall: Ceremonial county in England. Cornwall (Cornish: Kernow [ˈkɛrnɔʊ] or [ˈkɛrnɔ]) is a ceremonial county in South West England.

Effective altruism: Philosophical and social movement.

Erik the Red: Norse explorer. According to Icelandic sagas, Erik was born in the Jæren district of Rogaland, Norway, the son of Thorvald Asvaldsson.

Ferdinand Marcos: President of the Philippines from 1965 to 1986.

House of Habsburg: European dynastic family.

Javier Milei: President of Argentina since 2023. Javier Gerardo Milei (born 22 October 1970) is an Argentine politician and economist who has served as the 57th president of Argentina since 2023.
Born in tiny Neustadt, Ontario before his family moved west to what became Saskatchewan, this criminal-defence lawyer rose to become Canada's 13th prime minister from 1957 to 1963; who was he?
John Diefenbaker: Prime Minister of Canada from 1957 to 1963. John George Diefenbaker (September 18, 1895 – August 16, 1979) was the 13th prime minister of Canada, serving from 1957 to 1963.

Rising from vice president after Bingu wa Mutharika's death, she became the first female president of Malawi in 2012 and only the second woman to lead an African nation, after Liberia's Ellen Johnson Sirleaf — who is she?

Joyce Banda: President of Malawi from 2012 to 2014. Joyce Hilda Banda (née Ntila; born 12 April 1950) is a Malawian politician, educator, and activist who served as the fourth president of Malawi from 2012 to 2014.

Founded in 1892 by Filipino nationalists including Andrés Bonifacio, this revolutionary secret society was abbreviated KKK and sought independence from Spain, its 1896 discovery sparking a revolution — what was it called?
Katipunan: Filipino secret society during the Spanish colonization.

One of the original five Marshals of the Soviet Union, this military officer and politician later served as the country's head of state from 1953 to 1960, having forged a close friendship with Stalin during the Battle of Tsaritsyn — who was he?
Kliment Voroshilov: Soviet military officer and politician (1881–1969)
This Norse explorer is believed to have reached continental North America roughly five centuries before Columbus, establishing a settlement he called Vinland — who is he?
The younger brother of a French emperor, this monarch ruled the client Kingdom of Holland from 1806 to 1810 after marrying his own step-niece, the daughter of Empress Josephine — who was he?
Louis Bonaparte: King of Holland from 1806 to 1810. Louis Bonaparte (born Luigi Buonaparte; 2 September 1778 – 25 July 1846) was a younger brother of Napoleon I, Emperor of the French.
This Northern Irish peace activist co-founded a movement seeking a peaceful end to the Troubles, sharing the 1976 Nobel Peace Prize with Betty Williams — who is she?

Before becoming Italy's prime minister in 2021, this economist spent eight years as president of the European Central Bank — who is he?
Mario Draghi: Prime Minister of Italy from 2021 to 2022.

This young Arab commander, serving the Umayyad Caliphate, captured the region of Sindh around 712, marking the start of Muslim rule in South Asia — who is he?
Muhammad ibn al-Qasim: Umayyad general and governor of Sindh (695–715)

The principal wife of Ramesses the Great, this Egyptian queen was rare among her peers for being literate in hieroglyphs — a skill she used in royal diplomatic correspondence — and had her own temple built beside his at Abu Simbel. Who was she?
Nefertari: Wife of the Egyptian pharaoh Ramesses II.

Nyx: Ancient Greek goddess of the night. In ancient Greek art, Nyx often appears alongside other celestial deities such as Selene, Helios and Eos, as a winged figure driving a horse-pulled chariot.

Saul: Biblical figure and Israelite monarch.

Titus: Roman emperor from AD 79 to 81. Titus Flavius Vespasianus (30 December 39 – 13 September 81 AD) was Roman emperor from 79 to 81 AD.

Urartu: Iron-Age kingdom of the ancient Near East.

Founded by Grigory Yavlinsky and translating to 'Apple' in Russian, this social-liberal party held seats in the State Duma before losing its faction status in 2003 — which party?
Yabloko: Russian political party. The party consequently participated in the elections of deputies of the State Duma of the Federal Assembly of the Russian Federation of all eight convocations.

The first woman and youngest person ever to hold Slovakia's presidency, this lawyer and environmental activist won the 2016 Goldman Environmental Prize for fighting a toxic landfill in her hometown. Who is she?
Zuzana Čaputová: President of Slovakia from 2019 to 2024.
Who among these four was born earliest?
William Osler (born 1849) is the earliest of the four. Osler created the first residency program for specialty training of physicians.
Which of these four is the eldest?
Ada Lovelace (born 1815) is the earliest of the four. Lovelace is often considered the first computer programmer.
Which of these four dates back furthest?
MUMPS (founded 1966) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four began earliest?
Pascal (programming language) (founded 1970) is the earliest of the four. It is named after French mathematician, philosopher and physicist Blaise Pascal.
Who among these is a physicist?
Which one below is best known as a mathematician?
Ingrid Daubechies is a mathematician. Baroness Ingrid Daubechies ( doh-bə-SHEE; French: [dobʃi]; born 17 August 1954) is a Belgian-American physicist and mathematician at Duke University.
What is the atomic number of Copernicium?
Copernicium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Cn and atomic number 112.
What is the atomic number of Thallium?
Thallium is a chemical element; it has symbol Tl and atomic number 81.
In what year did Johann Wolfgang von Goethe die?
Johann Wolfgang von Goethe (28 August 1749 – 22 March 1832) was a German polymath who is widely regarded as the most influential writer in the German language.
In what year was Nitrogen discovered?
Nitrogen is a chemical element; it has symbol N and atomic number 7.
Which company manufactures Lockheed F-117 Nighthawk?
Lockheed F-117 Nighthawk: Skunk Works. It was the first operational aircraft to be designed with stealth technology.
Which country is Panavia Tornado from?
Panavia Tornado: Italy. It first flew on 14 August 1974 and was introduced into service in 1979–1980.
Who is credited with discovering Pavo?
Pavo (constellation): Petrus Plancius. Pavo is a constellation in the southern sky whose name is Latin for 'peacock'.
Who is credited with discovering Nitroglycerin?
Nitroglycerin: Ascanio Sobrero. It is combined with nitrocellulose to form double-based smokeless powder, used as a propellant in artillery and firearms since the 1880s.
Who is credited with discovering Lithium?
Lithium: Johan August Arfwedson. Lithium (from Ancient Greek: λίθος, líthos, 'stone') is a chemical element; it has symbol Li and atomic number 3.

The only living member of its entire taxonomic order, this nocturnal African mammal digs into termite and ant hills using sharp claws and powerful legs — related distantly to elephants and manatees, what is it?
Aardvark (Orycteropus afer) is a medium-sized, burrowing, nocturnal mammal native to Africa.
A pioneer of industrial toxicology, this American physician trained at Michigan, worked out of Hull House in Chicago, and led the fight to curb lead poisoning in the workplace — who was she?
Alice Hamilton (February 27, 1869 - September 22, 1970) was an American physician, research scientist, and author.
Nicknamed the 'nail mosquito,' this genus — first classified in 1818 — is the sole mosquito genus known to carry human malaria — which genus is it?
Anopheles is a genus of mosquito first described by the German entomologist J. W. Meigen in 1818.
About a third of the several hundred mold species in this genus have a sexual reproductive stage, and some cause infections while others hold commercial value — which genus?
Aspergillus is a genus consisting of several hundred mold species found in various climates worldwide.
Ranging from 1 to 5 meters tall and found across Europe, Asia, Africa and the Americas, this shrub genus's best-known species is the European type also called barberry — what genus is it?
Berberis is a large genus of deciduous and evergreen shrubs from 1-5 m (3+12-16+12 ft) tall, found throughout temperate and subtropical regions of the world (apart from Australia).
This branch of biology studies how plants have grown, reproduced, and evolved over the last 3.5 billion years of life on Earth — what field is it?
Botany is the branch of natural science and biology that studies the growth, reproduction and evolution of plants over the last 3.5 billion years of life on earth.

The largest land bird in North America went fully extinct in the wild in 1987 when every survivor was captured for breeding — which critically endangered vulture has since returned to the Grand Canyon and beyond?
California condor (Gymnogyps californianus) is a New World vulture and the largest North American land bird.

Appearing in early childhood with symptoms like poor coordination and stiff or weak muscles, this group of movement disorders does not worsen over time even though symptoms become more noticeable in a child's first years — which condition?
Cerebral palsy (CP) is a group of movement disorders that appear in early childhood.
This tangor — a mandarin-orange cross — typically splits into seven to fourteen easy-to-peel segments — which fruit?
Clementine (Citrus clementina) is a tangor, a citrus fruit hybrid between a willowleaf mandarin orange (C. deliciosa) and a sweet orange (C. sinensis).
Born in 1863, this Italian mathematician is remembered chiefly as a major contributor to the early development of algebraic geometry — who was he?
Corrado Segre (20 August 1863 - 18 May 1924) was an Italian mathematician who is remembered today as a major contributor to the early development of algebraic geometry.
Affecting some 280 million people worldwide, this state of low mood saps motivation and the pleasure once taken in activities — what is it?
Depression (mood) is a mental state of low mood and aversion to activity.
Sometimes triggered by lead poisoning or reactions to neuroleptic drugs, this neurological disorder produces involuntary, twisting muscle contractions — what is it?

Dystonia is a neurological hyperkinetic movement disorder in which sustained or repetitive muscle contractions occur involuntarily, resulting in twisting and repetitive movements or abnormal fixed postures.
This Ancient Greek polymath, who became chief librarian at the Library of Alexandria, is considered the founder of geography as a discipline and coined much of its early terminology — who is he?
The excessive buildup of collagen-rich connective tissue after chronic inflammation or repeated injury, leaving a permanent scar that can choke off organ function — what's this process called?
Fibrosis is the development of fibrous connective tissue in response to an injury.
Sometimes mistakenly called the 'stomach flu' even though it's unrelated to influenza, this inflammation of the gut is usually viral, with rotavirus the top cause in children. What condition is it?
Gastroenteritis is an inflammation of the gastrointestinal tract including the stomach and intestine.
The first of America's Teen Series fighters, this twin-tail jet with swing wings debuted at sea on the USS Enterprise in 1974. What is it?
Grumman F-14 Tomcat is an American carrier-capable supersonic, twin-engine, tandem two-seat, twin-tail, all-weather-capable variable-sweep wing fighter aircraft.
Nicknamed the giant crab spider or cane spider, this member of the huntsman spider family is native to the tropics but has spread into subtropical areas — what is it?
Heteropoda venatoria is a species of spider in the family Sparassidae, the huntsman spiders.
About the size of an almond in humans, this small brain region links the nervous system to the endocrine system via the pituitary gland — what is it?
Hypothalamus (pl.: hypothalami; from Ancient Greek (hup) 'under' and (thlamos) 'chamber') is a small part of the vertebrate brain that contains a number of nuclei with a variety of functions.
The biggest cat in the Americas, it kills with a bite so powerful it can crack a turtle's shell — or punch straight through a mammal's skull between the ears. Which spotted predator is it?
Jaguar (Panthera onca) is a large cat species and the only living member of the genus Panthera that is native to the Americas.
This Indian aerospace engineer served as secretary of the Department of Space and chairman of both ISRO and the Space Commission — who is he?
K. Sivan (born 14 April 1957) is an Indian aerospace engineer who served as the secretary of the Department of Space and chairman of ISRO and Space Commission.

Seen using a silver stain and grown on media containing the amino acid cysteine, this genus of bacteria causes a severe pneumonia-like illness as well as a milder flu-like illness called Pontiac fever — name the genus?
Legionella is a genus of Gram-negative bacteria that can be seen using a silver stain or grown in a special media that contains cysteine, an amino acid.

Fatigue, memory problems, breathlessness, and sleep trouble that the WHO marks as setting in three months after infection — symptoms that vanish and reappear for weeks or years. What condition is this?
Long COVID is a group of health problems persisting or developing after an initial period of COVID19 from 2 infection.
An autosomal dominant flaw in the fibrillin-making FBN1 gene gives this disorder its tell-tale look — tall, long-limbed, double-jointed — while quietly threatening the aorta — what is it?
Marfan syndrome (MFS) is a multi-systemic genetic disorder that affects the connective tissue.
This British-Lebanese geometer co-founded topological K-theory and lent his name to a famous index theorem — and won both the Fields Medal and the Abel Prize. Who was he?
Michael Atiyah (22 April 1929 - 11 January 2019) was a British-Lebanese mathematician specialising in geometry.

Though its 83 species can grow as tall as trees, this genus is technically herbaceous, its 'trunk' just tightly wrapped leaf stalks, and it gives us edible bananas, plantains, and fiber for cloth — what genus is it?
Musa (plant) is one of three genera in the family Musaceae.
This nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug treats acute pain and osteoarthritis by blocking prostaglandin production, though it carries a risk of liver side effects. Name the drug?
Nimesulide is a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) with pain medication and fever reducing properties.

Believed to be the world's fourth-leading cause of disability, this condition wears down joint cartilage over years, often first striking the knuckles nearest your fingertips and the base of the thumb — what is it?
Osteoarthritis is a type of degenerative joint disease that results from breakdown of joint cartilage and underlying bone.

Also known as underage medicine, this branch of medicine covers care from infancy through adolescence — typically up to age 18 in most of the Commonwealth, but only 12 in India. Name the medical specialty?

Pediatrics (American English), also spelled paediatrics (British English) and also known as underage medicine, is the branch of medicine that involves the medical care of infants, toddlers, children, adolescents, and young adults.
When this domesticated mammal reached Europe from the Near East, it interbred so freely with local wild boar that scholars still argue whether it's a distinct species — what animal is it?
Pig (Sus domesticus), also called swine (pl.: swine) or hog, is an omnivorous, domesticated, even-toed, hoofed mammal.

Caused by the loss of function of specific genes on chromosome 15, this rare genetic disorder leads to weak muscles and poor feeding in infancy, then constant hunger and risk of obesity in childhood — what's it called?

Prader–Willi syndrome (PWS) is a rare genetic disorder caused by a loss of function of specific genes on chromosome 15. A similar mechanism occurs in Angelman syndrome, except the defective chromosome 15 is from the mother, or two copies are from the father.
This white, odorless nitroamine explosive, widely used since World War II, is the explosive agent inside C-4 plastic explosive — what is it called?
RDX (Research Department Explosive or Royal Demolition Explosive), or hexogen, also known by other names, is an organic compound with the formula (CH2N2O2)3.
Made by steaming dehusked oat groats before flattening them under heavy rollers and lightly toasting them, this whole-grain food becomes porridge when cooked — which product?
Rolled oats are a type of lightly processed whole-grain food.
Caused by a lack of vitamin C, this deficiency disease shows up after about a month of poor diet with weakness, sore limbs, gum disease, and bleeding from the skin — what is it?
Scurvy is a deficiency disease (state of malnutrition) resulting from a lack of vitamin C (ascorbic acid).
Unlike its shelled cousin the snail, this soft-bodied land mollusk gets by with no shell at all, or at most a tiny internal remnant of one — what animal is it?
Slug is a common name for any apparently shell-less terrestrial gastropod mollusc.
This Taiwanese-American software engineer co-founded and served as CTO of a massively popular video-sharing platform before later building MixBit through his company AVOS Systems — who is he?
Steve Chen (Wade-; born August 25, 1978) is a Taiwanese-American software engineer and Internet entrepreneur who is a co-founder and ex-CTO of YouTube.
Defined as applying conceptual knowledge to reach practical goals in a repeatable way, this field covers both tangible machines and intangible things like software — what is it?
Technology is the application of conceptual knowledge to achieve practical goals, especially in a reproducible way.
What's the name for hardened, foul-smelling deposits of trapped debris that form in the crevices of the tonsils, sometimes visible as white flecks at the back of the throat?
Tonsil stones are mineralizations of debris within the crevices of the tonsils.
Occasionally causing hearing loss or bone marrow suppression as side effects, this IV antibiotic treats MRSA infections and, in oral form, a common gut infection - which drug?
Vancomycin is a glycopeptide antibiotic medication used to treat certain bacterial infections.
Short-legged, muscular, and stubby-tailed, this Australian marsupial can reach about a metre long and tip the scales between 20 and 35 kilograms — what is it?
Wombat are short-legged, muscular quadrupedal marsupials of the family Vombatidae that are native to Australia.
Found naturally in coffee, bread and ripe fruit, this aldehyde is produced when your liver partly oxidizes ethanol — making it a chief culprit behind the hangover. What is it?

Born as a Spanish CASA design and now built by a major European aerospace conglomerate, this twin-engine turboprop transport plane first flew in November 1997 and entered Spanish Air Force service in 1999 — which aircraft?
Airbus C295: European tactical military transport aircraft.
Nicknamed the death cap, this deadly poisonous fungus resembles edible species like Caesar's mushroom and is native to Europe — what is it?
Amanita phalloides: Poisonous mushroom (death cap). The large fruiting bodies appear in summer and autumn; the caps are generally greenish in colour with a white stipe and gills.
Native to the eastern Mediterranean, this flowering herb's seeds taste similar to fennel, licorice, and tarragon and flavor candies and spirits — what is it?
Also called gobō, this Eurasian plant is cultivated in Japan for its edible root but has become an invasive weed of high-nitrogen soils elsewhere — which species?
Arctium lappa: Species of flowering plant. It has become an invasive weed of high-nitrogen soils in North America, Australia, and other regions, but is cultivated for its vegetable root.
An aurora glows when charged particles from the Sun collide with which two gases high in Earth's atmosphere?
The collisions excite oxygen and nitrogen atoms, which release the energy as light -- oxygen gives the familiar green and red, nitrogen the blues and purples.
Making up nearly 40% of all known insects with around 400,000 described species, this order is distinguished by front wings hardened into protective cases called elytra — what creatures are these?
Beetle: Order of insects. Over 300 species are used as food, mostly as larvae; species widely consumed include mealworms and rhinoceros beetle larvae.

Despite its name, this African animal's hide actually ranges from brown to grey, and it's distinguished from its 'white' cousin by a pointed, hooked upper lip rather than a wide, square one — which species?
Black rhinoceros: Species of mammal. Although the species is referred to as black, its colours vary from brown to grey.
Named for its unusually long forelimbs — Greek for 'arm lizard' — this Late Jurassic sauropod was first described in 1903 from fossils found in Colorado — which dinosaur?
Brachiosaurus: Sauropod dinosaur genus from the late Jurassic Period.
Caused by the SARS-CoV-2 virus, this global pandemic began with an outbreak in December 2019 in which Chinese city?
The global COVID-19 pandemic, caused by severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), began with an outbreak in Wuhan, China, in December 2019, spreading worldwide in early 2020.

This group of heart-muscle diseases includes the 'broken heart syndrome' type and can lead to irregular heartbeats, fainting, or even sudden cardiac death — what's the general term for this condition?
Cardiomyopathy: Disease of the heart muscle. In dilated cardiomyopathy the ventricles enlarge and weaken.
Also known as an ischemic stroke, this necrotic brain condition is the second-leading cause of death worldwide and a leading cause of physical disability — what is it?
Cerebral infarction: Stroke resulting from lack of blood flow.
This class of jawed fish — including sharks, rays, skates, and ghost-like chimaeras — has skeletons made entirely of cartilage rather than bone — what is it called?
Chondrichthyes: Class of jawed cartilaginous fish. Chondrichthyes are aquatic vertebrates with paired fins, paired nares, placoid scales, and conus arteriosus in the heart.
Nicknamed the 'palm thief,' this giant terrestrial arthropod can weigh over 9 pounds, making it the largest land-dwelling arthropod alive today — what is it?
Thanks to a variation in the gene OR6A2, some people taste this herb — called cilantro in the US — as fresh and citrusy while others swear it tastes like soap. What is it?
Coriander: Annual herb. Coriander, or Coriandrum sativum, is an annual herb in the family Apiaceae.
Its Greek name literally means 'boat beard,' describing how its hairy spikelets project from boat-shaped sheaths — better known by a common name evoking a citrus scent, what is this grass genus?
First patented in Germany in 1920 and later synthesized by an American chemist in 1932, this semi-synthetic opioid is roughly ten times more potent than morphine — what is it called?
Desomorphine: Semi-synthetic opioid, morphine analogue. It was first discovered and patented in Germany by a German team working for Knoll in 1920 but was not generally recognized.
Despite its common names, this evergreen conifer isn't a true member of the pine, spruce, or hemlock genera, yet stands as the tallest species in its own family — what is it?
Douglas fir: Species of tree. It is native to western North America and is also known as Douglas-fir, Douglas spruce, Oregon pine, and Columbian pine.

A subfield of physics and electrical engineering, this discipline uses transistors, diodes, and integrated circuits to control and amplify current — and to convert AC to DC or analog to digital — what is it?

Electronics: Branch of physics and electrical engineering. The semiconductor industry is one of the global economy's largest and most profitable industries, with annual revenues exceeding $481 billion in 2018.
About 60 to 70 percent as sweet as table sugar yet virtually calorie-free, this sugar alcohol is fermented from corn and was commercially pioneered by Japanese companies in the 1990s — what is it?
Erythritol: Sugar alcohol that is used as a sweetener.
Sporting a dark facial mask and famous for a seriously foul-smelling territorial secretion, this stocky mustelid ranges across the continent and Morocco's Rif mountains — which species is it?
Belonging to the genus Abies, these evergreen conifers have cones that stand upright like candles and disintegrate at maturity, and some varieties serve as Christmas trees — which conifer genus?
Fir: Genus of coniferous trees. The genus is most closely related to Keteleeria, a small genus confined to eastern Asia.
Often bonded to glucose to form sucrose, this simple sugar is found in honey, fruit, and most root vegetables — which sugar?
Fructose: Simple ketonic monosaccharide found in many plants.

Among the longest of all living crocodilians, this fish-eater wields a slender snout lined with 110 interlocking teeth, and the males sport a bulbous, pot-shaped bump on the tip that gives the animal its name. What is it?
Gharial: Crocodilian native to the Indian subcontinent.
This branch of discrete mathematics studies structures made of vertices connected by edges, modeling pairwise relationships between objects — what field is it?

Graph theory: Area of discrete mathematics. In mathematics and computer science, graph theory is the study of graphs, which are mathematical structures used to model pairwise relations between objects.

This British aviation entrepreneur held three Guinness World Records after visiting the South Pole, the Challenger Deep, and space, then died in 2023 aboard the submersible that imploded near the Titanic wreck — who was he?
Also known as the cane spider or giant crab spider, this huntsman species native to the tropics has spread to subtropical regions worldwide — what is it?
Heteropoda venatoria: Species of spider. It is native to the tropical regions of the world, and it is present in some subtropical areas as an introduced species.
Marketed as Hydrodiuril, this medication treats high blood pressure and fluid retention by blocking sodium and chloride reabsorption in the kidneys' distal tubules — what drug is it?

Hydrochlorothiazide: Diuretic medication. Hydrochlorothiazide, sold under the brand name Hydrodiuril among others, is a diuretic medication used to treat hypertension and swelling due to fluid build-up.
First described to Europeans in 1812, this reddish-brown African antelope's males sport lyre-shaped horns up to three feet long — which animal?
Impala: Species of antelope found in Africa.

This Scottish physicist's equations unified electricity, magnetism, and light into a single theory — the second great unification in physics after Newton's — while also helping found statistical mechanics — who is he?
James Clerk Maxwell: Scottish physicist and mathematician (1831–1879)
Struggling with a morphine addiction from a Civil War saber wound, this pharmacist and chemist developed a coca-and-caffeine beverage in 1886 that became Coca-Cola — who is he?
John Stith Pemberton: American pharmacist, inventor of Coca-Cola (1831–1888)
A biologist and botanist married four times — her last husband directed the Manhattan Project's Los Alamos lab — she was played by Emily Blunt in a 2023 film. Who was she?
Its lens-shaped seeds, usually two to a pod, are split and simmered into the dal that's a staple across the Indian subcontinent — which legume?
Lentil: Species of plant with edible seeds.
Nicknamed "Connie" and instantly recognizable by its triple tail and dolphin-shaped fuselage, which four-engined airliner was the first civil aircraft family to widely use a pressurized cabin?
Lockheed Constellation: Family of US airliners with 4 piston engines, 1943.
This marsupial family native to Australia and New Guinea includes kangaroos, wallabies, and the quokka among its 63 recognized species — what is it?
Macropodidae: Family of marsupial mammals. Macropodidae is a family of marsupials that includes kangaroos, wallabies, tree-kangaroos, wallaroos, pademelons, the quokka, and several other groups.
A Zainichi Korean entrepreneur, this founder and CEO of SoftBank turned a $20 million bet on Alibaba in 2000 into a stake worth around $75 billion — who is he?
Developed in 1955 and later sold under the brand name Dianabol, this anabolic steroid was once widely used for physique and performance enhancement — what is it?
Metandienone: Androgen and anabolic steroid. It is also used non-medically for physique- and performance-enhancing purposes.
Normally equal to 60 seconds, which unit of time has occasionally run 61 seconds long in UTC due to leap seconds, though a 59-second version has never actually occurred?
Minute: Unit of time equal to 60 seconds. The prime symbol ′ is also sometimes used informally to denote minutes.
Also known as green gram, this legume is a staple ingredient across East, Southeast, and South Asian cuisine in both savory and sweet dishes — what is it?
Discovered in 1898 alongside krypton and xenon, this noble gas gets its name from the Greek word for 'new' and glows bright red in electrical discharge — what element is it?
Neon: Chemical element with atomic number 10 (Ne)
This Turkish-born American economist, a Harvard-trained NYU professor, earned lasting fame as one of the few who foresaw the 2008 subprime mortgage crisis. Who is he?
With atomic number 76 and symbol Os, this bluish-white transition metal has the highest density of any stable element and was once prized for fountain-pen nib tips — what is it?
Osmium: Chemical element with atomic number 76 (Os). Osmium (from Ancient Greek ὀσμή (osmḗ) 'smell') is a chemical element; it has symbol Os and atomic number 76.

First described by a 17th-century French mathematician in 1653, this fluid mechanics principle states that a pressure change at any point in a confined, incompressible fluid is felt equally throughout it — what's it called?
Pascal's law: Principle in fluid mechanics. The law was established by French mathematician Blaise Pascal in 1653 and published in 1663.
Named from a Tupi-Guarani word for tobacco filtered through French, this South American flowering plant genus is a garden hybrid favorite — which plant?
Petunia: Genus of flowering plants. The popular flower of the same name derived its epithet from the French, which took the word pétun, 'tobacco', from a Tupi–Guarani language.

Often stereotyped as ferocious predators, these South American freshwater fish actually have varied diets that include plant matter, making them more omnivorous than their reputation suggests. What fish are they?
Piranha: Common name for certain fishes of the family Serrasalmidae.
Chickens, turkeys, ducks, and geese all fall under this term for birds domesticated for meat, eggs, or feathers — what is it called?
Poultry: Domesticated birds kept by humans for their eggs, meat or feathers.
Forming the front-most part of the hip bone in vertebrates, this structure is made up of a superior ramus, an inferior ramus, and a body — which bone?
Pubis: Most forward-facing of the three main regions making up the os coxa.
Roughly 12 centimeters long in adults, this final section of the large intestine temporarily stores waste before it passes into the anal canal — what is it?
Rectum: Final portion of the large intestine. The rectum (pl.: rectums or recta) is the final straight portion of the large intestine in humans and some other mammals, and the gut in others.
Having spent years building theremins, this engineer debuted the first commercial synthesizer in 1964 and later the portable Minimoog — earning a spot in the Inventors Hall of Fame. Who is it?
Robert Moog: American electronic music pioneer (1934–2005)

The largest living reptile, whose males can top 1,000 kg and stretch six metres, ranges from India's coast through Southeast Asia to northern Australia — and earns its 'dangerous to humans' reputation. Which croc is it?
Saltwater crocodile: Species of reptile. It has been listed as Least Concern on the IUCN Red List since 1996.
As chief technology officer of a Turkish defense company, this pilot-engineer designed Turkey's first indigenous unmanned combat aerial vehicle and its first unmanned fighter jet. Who is he?
Selçuk Bayraktar: Turkish engineer and businessman. Selçuk Bayraktar (born 7 October 1979) is a Turkish pilot, engineer and businessman.
Related to polecats but more closely kin to the Old World stink badgers, these black-and-white mammals defend themselves by spraying a foul-smelling liquid from their anal glands — which animal?
Skunk: Common name of mammals in the family Mephitidae.
Acting as a blood filter and red-blood-cell recycling center, which vertebrate organ also stores a reserve of blood for use during hemorrhagic shock?
Spleen: Immune organ that filters blood.
Codenamed 'Flanker' by NATO, this Soviet twin-engine fighter entered service in 1985 as an air-superiority answer to the F-14 and F-15 — what is it?
Sukhoi Su-27: Soviet 4th generation fighter aircraft.
This Japanese immunologist shared the 2018 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine with James P. Allison for identifying the PD-1 protein — who is he?
Tasuku Honjo: Japanese immunologist and Nobel laureate (born 1942)
With a half-life of roughly 14 billion years — about the age of the universe — the most stable isotope of this weakly radioactive metal decays into stable lead-208. Which element is it?
Thorium: Chemical element with atomic number 90 (Th)
Botanically a perennial with an elongated trunk, this form isn't a single family — palms, ferns, and bamboos all independently grew tall stems to win at chasing sunlight. What is it?
Tree: Perennial woody plant with elongated trunk.
A breakdown product of purine nucleotides found naturally in urine, elevated blood levels of this heterocyclic compound can trigger gout and kidney stones — what is it?
Uric acid: Organic compound. Uric acid is a heterocyclic compound of carbon, nitrogen, oxygen, and hydrogen with the formula C5H4N4O3.
Comprising the mons pubis, labia, clitoris, and vaginal opening, these external structures of the female genitalia are supplied by the pudendal arteries. What is this collectively called?
Vulva: External genitalia of the female mammal. The folds of the outer and inner labia provide a double layer of protection for the vagina (which leads to the uterus).

A physician by training, this Polish politician has served as Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Defence since 2023, after leading his country's labour ministry a decade earlier — who is he?
Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz: Polish physician and politician (born 1981)
What is the chemical symbol for neptunium?
The symbol for neptunium is Np. Neptunium is a chemical element; it has symbol Np and atomic number 93.
Europium is denoted by which symbol?
The symbol for europium is Eu. Europium is a chemical element; it has symbol Eu and atomic number 63.

Sebastian Maniscalco is a comedian. Sebastian Maniscalco (Italian: [maniˈskalko]; born July 8, 1973) is an American stand-up comedian and actor.
In what year was Rachel Weisz born?
Rachel Weisz: Rachel Hannah Weisz (born 7 March 1970) is a British actress.
In what year was Sarah Jessica Parker born?
Sarah Jessica Parker (born March 25, 1965) is an American actress and television producer.
In what year was Rachel McAdams born?
Rachel McAdams: Rachel Anne McAdams (born November 17, 1978) is a Canadian actress.
In what year was Natasha Richardson born?
Natasha Richardson: Natasha Jane Richardson (11 May 1963 – 18 March 2009) was an English actress.
In what year was Hrithik Roshan born?
Hrithik Roshan: Roshan has frequently collaborated with his father, Rakesh Roshan.
In what year was Paul Rudd born?
